title: Daily Debrief — Tuesday Nov 10, 2026
html:
A hot inflation report tested SPY's $745 floor, and the floor held.

Here's what I'm seeing. Prices rose faster than expected in October and bond yields hit 5%, but SPY dipped to its floor and bounced. Nvidia, not inflation, did most of the damage today.

The one thing

SPY's $744–745 floor held a hot CPI. Above it, the SPY call stays on. A close under $744 says the floor is cracking.

Core CPI (inflation without food and energy) rose 0.3% in October against 0.2% expected, the third month in a row at that pace. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped about 0.14 points to 5.00%, and Fed Governor Waller had said a 0.3% core reading makes a half-point December hike worth weighing.

Yet SPY only slipped 0.4% to $749.92. Its low, $744.86, landed on the floor and buyers stepped in. The real drag was Nvidia, down 5.5% to $168.89 on the investigation into its CEO, which pulled the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) down 0.7% while the Dow lost only 0.3%.

The market in one picture: SPY

  • Oct 6 record high: $781.62
  • Ceiling · 61.8% + 20 & 50-day: $761–765
  • 50% of the drop · target 1: $757.17
  • 38.2% · today's stall: $751.39
  • The floor · 23.6% + old floor: $744–745
  • Nov 5 low · call stop $732: $732.71
  • 200-day + 38.2% of big run: $722–728
  • 50% of the Mar–Oct run: $703.87
  • Now: $749.92

How I read it: today the 38.2% line at $751.39 capped the bounce (high $752.14) and the floor at $744–745 caught the dip. SPY is boxed in a $7 range. A close above $751.39 opens $757.17. A close below $744 and I turn defensive, with the Nov 5 low $732.71 next.

Your names that matter today

Why these names: DAL and PLTR carry live plays (an open call and a waiting trigger), and Nvidia made the biggest move on the list and reports in a week.

  • The chart: Strong but stretched: RSI 67, and 13% above its 20-day average ($81.51). If it rests, the first support is the 23.6% pullback of the Oct 20 → Nov 10 run at $88.18. The golden pocket $81.16–83.33 sits under your stop.
  • Watching: Target 2 is $95.18, the 52-week high: take profit there. Stop: DAL below $83. No new DAL calls up here, we already own one.

  • BA $173.38 · +0.6%. Eleven sessions stuck between $165 and $179. Nothing to do until $165 breaks or a rally fails at $179–181.5. The $170 put is $545, FAIR.

Lesson of the day: Rates are gravity: why a 5% bond yield pulls hardest on growth stocks

A stock is worth the profits it will earn in the future, translated into today's dollars. When a safe 10-year Treasury pays 5%, a dollar of profit ten years from now is worth less today than when bonds paid 4%. Fast-growing tech companies earn most of their profit far in the future, so they lose the most value when yields jump. Companies earning steady money now lose less.

  • 10-year yield: 5.00% (up about 0.14 points today)
  • Nasdaq 100 vs Dow: −0.7% / −0.3% (growth fell more)

You could see it all over the board today. TLT, the long-bond fund, fell 1.3% (bond prices fall when yields rise). Coca-Cola rose 0.9% and Lockheed 2.5%. What it means for you: while the 10-year sits near 5% and the Fed talks about hikes, keep growth-stock calls small, wait for the trigger, and give extra weight to names that earn money now.

    • Why: The reclaim of the $745 floor held through CPI. This is a hold, not a new entry. Enter: opened intraday at $450.50 with SPY at $748.90. Exit: SPY below $732. Targets: $757, then $762–765.
    • OI 44,459 · vol 28,781 · bid/ask $4.77/$4.83 (1% spread) · delta 0.26 · IV 13% vs moves 15% → CHEAP · no earnings inside

A second DAL call up here: we already own one, and it has run 24% from the Oct 20 low. HLT $390 and LMT calls: too thin and over $800.

Homework

  1. Mark $744–745 and $751.39 on your SPY chart. Today's candle touched both. Tomorrow's close tells us which side wins.
  2. On NVDA's daily chart, find the Mar 30 low ($163.90). Watch whether the next few candles defend it or slice through before earnings.

SPY has a floor at $745 and a ceiling at $751. If it closes at $743 tomorrow, what do you do with the SPY $775 call, whose stop is $732?

Set these alerts

  • PLTR — price crosses above $172.23 → call trigger
  • BA — price crosses below $165.00 → put trigger
  • DAL — price crosses above $95.18 → target 2, take profit on the $90 call
  • HLT — price crosses above $385.93 → target 1 on the $380 call (sell with a limit)
  • SPY — price crosses below $744.00 → the floor is cracking; review the SPY call

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Fib in action · Retracements 101 (Fibonacci Playbook)

Measuring a bounce inside a drop: SPY's 38.2% line

A retracement measures how much of a move gets taken back. After a drop, you anchor on the high and the low, and the bounce tends to stall at 23.6%, 38.2%, 50% or 61.8% of the way back.

Anchors: the Oct 6 record high $781.62 and the Nov 5 low $732.71, the two clearest turns. Range = $48.91. Math: level = low + range × ratio. 23.6% = 732.71 + 48.91 × 0.236 = $744.25. 38.2% = 732.71 + 48.91 × 0.382 = $751.39. 50% = $757.17. 61.8% = $762.94.

What price did: today's high $752.14 poked above the 38.2% and closed under it at $749.92 (a wick). The low $744.86 held the 23.6%. For the trade: a close over $751.39 points to $757.17 (target 1); the stop at $732 sits under the 0% line. The $775 strike sits just above the 78.6% ($771.15), so it needs nearly the whole drop taken back to finish in the money.

Ladder:

  • Oct 6 high (100% back): $781.62
  • 78.6%: $771.15
  • 61.8%: $762.94
  • 50%: $757.17
  • 38.2% · today's high wicked it: $751.39
  • 23.6% · today's low held: $744.25
  • Nov 5 low (0%): $732.71
  • Now: $749.92

Try it: QQQ fell from its Oct 28 high $726.14 to its Nov 5 low $647.05. Where's the 38.2%, and did today close above it?
